I hit a very similar problem specifically in Cursor's extension marketplace, which appears to use Open VSX listings.

When I searched for `opencode`, I saw this listing:
https://open-vsx.org/extension/ZiShuo/opencode

and also this one:
https://open-vsx.org/extension/sst-dev/opencode

From a normal user's perspective, this is confusing for a few reasons:
- both listings use the same `opencode` name
- the unofficial-looking one is close enough in naming/description to be mistaken for the official extension
- the docs tell users to search by name, but do not clearly say which publisher/namespace is official
- in Cursor/Open VSX, users may not know that `sst-dev` is the correct publisher to trust

So this is not only a docs clarity issue, but also a trust/safety issue: users can plausibly install the wrong extension just by following the current instructions.

A direct link to the official marketplace listing plus an explicit publisher name would help a lot.

To be honest, I think the fix is much simpler. Using `bun info` is fine. It's just the implementation that's broken. It tries to read stdout and stderr of a stream after it has already exited, which does not work. So you always run into the
```
Failed to resolve latest version, using cached
```
case.

The fix is simple: Read stdout and stderr before the stream exits. The same approach is used in `Process.run` in `process.ts`:
```ts
    const [code, stdout, stderr] = await Promise.all([proc.exited, buffer(proc.stdout), buffer(proc.stderr)])
```

I'll create a minimal PR to fix this bug.

Reproducing a frequent hang on OpenCode v1.2.24 in a real iOS monorepo (Tuist workspace).

Project structure/context:
- repo root: `<your-repo-root>`
- feature path: `Features/<Feature>/Sources/Scene/<Scene>/`
- read targets:
  - `<PrimaryView>.swift` (~200-300 lines, ~8KB)
  - `View/<OverlayView>.swift` (~200-250 lines, ~7KB)
  - `<ViewModel>.swift` (~300-400 lines, ~12KB)

Trigger pattern:
1. Glob `Features/<Feature>/Sources/Scene/<Scene>/**/*.swift`
2. Glob `Features/<Feature>/Sources/Scene/<Scene>/**/*`
3. Read the 3 files above

Observed:
- session stays `running` indefinitely with no progress
- Esc/Esc usually recovers
- repro session metrics in my case: 200+ parts, 20+ `read` calls

Given this is a small-file read workflow (not large-file patching), this seems consistent with this issue class.

+1 from real usage: in the same repro flow, UI keeps showing `running` with no actionable error or stack.

Behavior in practice:
- tool chain appears to stop at the Glob -> Read boundary
- no surfaced tool-error in normal UI flow
- only Esc/Esc breaks out

Please surface full tool-error stack (or a direct log pointer) in-session when this happens.
Without that, this failure mode looks like a random freeze and is hard to triage in real project structures.

Hi @timrichardson, thanks for the thoughtful suggestion! 🙏

While the `experimental.chat.system.transform` hook is an interesting approach, I'd like to clarify why this PR takes a different direction:

1. **Internal integration over external hooks** — Since skill awareness is core to how opencode operates, it belongs inside the application's own logic rather than relying on a hook that users need to configure externally. A hook-based approach puts the burden on the user/operator, whereas this PR makes it work out of the box for everyone.

2. **Scope is broader than system prompt** — This PR doesn't only touch the system prompt. The changes span:
   - The **system prompt** — adds a short skill usage hint
   - The **user message (first turn)** — injects the `<system-reminder>` block with the skill list into conversation context
   - The **SkillTool description** — simplified to point models to the injected reminder instead of duplicating the list

   A `system.transform` hook alone wouldn't cover the user-message injection or the SkillTool description refinement.

3. **Hooks are experimental** — Building a core feature on top of an experimental API introduces fragility. If the hook interface changes, skill discovery would break silently.

The goal here is reliable, zero-config skill invocation as a first-class feature of opencode — not an opt-in extension. Happy to discuss further if you have concerns! 😊

The grep, glob, and list tools in opencode use ripgrep under the hood. You can check if ripgrep is installed. If not, opencode will try to install it automatically from the internet, and if that fails, this error may occur. You can try installing ripgrep manually and then give it another go — after I installed ripgrep, the error no longer occurred.
